name: rm-compat-mode
details:
Implementation plan for adding rm-compatible mode to rip2.

The goal is to modify rip to detect when it's invoked as 'rm' (via symlink) and behave 100% like GNU rm while maintaining backward compatibility with existing rip behavior.

This session focuses on PREPARATION ONLY - no implementation yet.

tasks.name: Analysis
tasks.details: Analyze GNU rm source code and rip2 codebase to understand architecture and identify what needs to be modified

sub_tasks.name: Study rm.c behavior
sub_tasks.details:
Deep dive into rm.c from GNU coreutils v9.4:
- Command-line parsing (getopt_long)
- Interactive prompting logic (RMI_NEVER/SOMETIMES/ALWAYS)
- Preserve-root protection
- Verbose output format
- Error handling and exit codes

sub_tasks.name: Map rip2 architecture
sub_tasks.details:
Use lsp-cli-file to understand rip2's current structure:
- main.rs: entry point and CLI parsing
- How rip currently handles deletion
- Graveyard management code
- Current interactive mode (-i flag conflict)

sub_tasks.name: Identify incompatibilities
sub_tasks.details:
Create detailed list of behavior differences:
- Flag conflicts (rip -i vs rm -i)
- Missing rm features (verbose, preserve-root, one-file-system, etc.)
- Different default behaviors
- Exit code differences
- Prompt message format differences

tasks.name: Design
tasks.details: Design the rm-compatibility architecture without writing code yet

sub_tasks.name: Binary name detection
sub_tasks.details:
Design how rip detects invocation mode:
- Check argv[0] for 'rm' suffix
- Environment variable override option?
- --rm-compat explicit flag as backup

sub_tasks.name: CLI argument mapping
sub_tasks.details:
Map all rm flags to rip behavior:
- -f, --force → disable prompts, ignore errors
- -i → interactive always (conflicts with current rip -i!)
- -I → interactive once
- --interactive=WHEN → parse never/once/always
- -r, -R, --recursive → enable recursive
- -d, --dir → remove empty dirs
- -v, --verbose → show each removal
- --preserve-root[=all] → protect /
- --no-preserve-root → allow /
- --one-file-system → stay on same filesystem

sub_tasks.name: Behavioral changes
sub_tasks.details:
Define how behavior changes in rm-compat mode:
- Prompting logic (when to ask user)
- Error messages format
- Exit codes (SUCCESS=0, ERROR=1)
- Verbose output format
- Root protection mechanism

sub_tasks.name: Backward compatibility
sub_tasks.details:
Ensure existing rip usage still works:
- All current rip flags work when invoked as 'rip'
- No breaking changes to rip behavior
- Clear separation between rip-mode and rm-mode
